postText:
Claude learned a new skill by watching someone do it once.

Not prompted. Not fine-tuned. Just shown, once, and then it could do it.

That's the one that stuck with me this week. Everything else was noise. Opus 5 beat their own flagship at half the price, ChatGPT can run your computer, Google dropped three models in a day. All of it happened in like seven days.

But record-a-skill is different. You show Claude a task, it watches, and now it knows. That's not a smarter model. That's a different kind of thing.

I keep thinking about what that means if you're building with agents. Right now training something new takes time and setup. This makes it feel more like onboarding a person? Show once, it learns. Weird to even type that.

Still don't fully get the limits of it. How fragile is the skill after recording. Whether it generalises or breaks the second context shifts a little.

If you've actually tried it, curious what happened.

#AI #BuildingWithAI #AgentDev
